record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: How should robustness of a social or networked system be related to systemic-risk measures, especially when systemic risk can arise not only from rare external shocks but also from internal failure cascades amplified through network structure and dynamics?

evidence.quote: Questions • How is robustness related to existing systemic risk measures?

Quantifying the impact of shocks requires to model the system’s response. Only such models allow to estimate whether large parts of the system will be destroyed, which is commonly denoted as systemic risk.
Tounderstand amplifying mechanisms inside a systems, we need models for the dynamics inside the nodes, but also models for the exchange of quantities between nodes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a networked system modeled as a (possibly time-varying) graph G = (V, E) in which each node i ∈ V carries an internal state x_i(t) evolving according to a prescribed dynamics, and in which interactions along edges (i, j) ∈ E permit the exchange of quantities between nodes and can propagate failures. A node is said to have "failed" at time t if its state lies in a designated failure set F_i ⊂ State_i. Let S(t) ⊂ V denote the set of failed nodes at time t.

Define:
(a) A robustness functional R(G, dynamics) that quantifies the system's ability to maintain functionality (e.g., to keep |S(t)|/|V| below a threshold, or to return to a reference state) when subjected to perturbations of either (i) exogenous type — rare external shocks applied to a subset of nodes or edges — or (ii) endogenous type — internal failure cascades triggered by individual node failures and amplified through the network topology and the inter-node dynamics.
(b) A systemic-risk measure ρ(G, dynamics) drawn from the class of measures used for interconnected systems (for example, monetary risk measures applied to aggregate losses Σ_i L_i, or CoVaR/Shapley-type allocations, or expected fraction of failed nodes under a stress scenario), which assigns a real number quantifying the risk that "large parts of the system are destroyed."

Problem. Provide a precise mathematical relationship between R and ρ within a single modeling framework that simultaneously accounts for:
1. exogenous rare-shock contributions to systemic risk, and
2. endogenous cascade contributions arising from the coupling of intra-node dynamics with inter-node exchange along the network.

Specifically: construct a class of dynamic network models for which one can prove inequalities, monotonicity relations, or functional identities linking R(G, dynamics) and ρ(G, dynamics), and identify network and dynamical conditions under which high robustness is equivalent to, implies, or is independent of low systemic risk.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open conceptual/modeling problem about how to formally connect robustness of networked systems with systemic-risk measures, including endogenous cascade effects. No single, universally accepted formal correspondence has emerged; the literature offers many partial frameworks (DebtRank, CoVaR, percolation thresholds, cascade models) but no unifying theorem linking robustness functionals and systemic-risk measures across both exogenous and endogenous shocks. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as an open question how robustness is related to existing systemic risk measures, noting that systemic risk arises from both external shocks and internal cascades.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between robustness and systemic-risk measures in networked systems is listed among open problems.
